This script is for calculating trait values from the segmented copepod images.

This file replaces parts of a few deprecated files including UPV6_lipidscape_analysis.Rmd and lipid and biomass concentrations UVP.Rmd.


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# Load libraries and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)

load("data/uvp6_CNN_segmentations_morphotraits_20251125.RData")

theme_set(theme_bw() +
            theme(text = element_text(size=14)))
source("functions/lipid_pump_toolkit.R")

# TODO Note that the excluded images can be filtered out here. OR NOT if we want to inspect how bad their derived traits are.
segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  filter(is_size_extrapolated == F & 
           is_bad_image == F)
```


# Convert pixels to traits
## Derive volume, dry weight, and carbon
```{r}
uvpRes <- 0.073
# Conversion factor to get total lipid mg C from total lipid mg used in Schmidt et al. 2018 based on 36-carbon chain lengths in (Kattner & Graeve 1991) 
lambda <- (36*12) / (36*12 + 2*36 + 2*16)
# Conversion factor to get prosome biomass (mg C) from biovolume (mm3)
vol2massC <- mean(c(0.14373,0.1177,0.1902)) # average of 3 Calanus species in (McConville et al. (2016)

# *** For the CNN segmented images ***
segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  # Convert pixel area to mm2
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome * uvpRes * uvpRes) %>% 
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome * uvpRes * uvpRes) %>% 
  
  mutate(prosome_length_mm = prosomeMajor * uvpRes) %>% # based on segmentation
  
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis (in pixels)
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome / (pi * prosomeMajor/2)) * 2) %>% 
  mutate(minor_lipid_derived = (lipid / (pi * lipidMajor/2)) * 2) %>% 
  
  
  # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * (prosomeMajor/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation. According to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipidMajor * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
  # # Calculate lipid sac volume based spheroid (results in slightly larger volume)
  # mutate(lipid_volume_mm3_sph = 
  #          4/3 * pi * (lipidMajor/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_lipid_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2))

  
  # Calculate lipid fullness based on volume
  mutate(lipidfullness_volume  = (lipid_volume_mm3/prosome_biovolume_mm3 * 100)) %>% 
  
  # (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. 2010 with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
  
  # TODO CLARIFY Calculate prosome carbon weight (** NOTE: many options ***)

  # Option 1: Use prosome length to volume (mm3) and calculate dry weight and mg C (Jonasdottir et al. 2019 for C. finmarchicus)
  mutate(prosome_volume_Jonasdottir = 
           0.0292 * (prosomeMajor * uvpRes)^3.6699,
         prosome_dryweight_Jonasdottir = 
           0.0106 * (prosomeMajor * uvpRes)^3.64,
         prosome_mgC_Jonasdottir = 
           0.623 * prosome_dryweight_Jonasdottir - 0.0143) %>% 
  
    # Option 2: Direct biovolume --> carbon mass based on conversion factors in McConville et al. 2016 assuming 1 mm3 = 1 mg wet weight
  mutate(prosome_mgC_McConville = 
           prosome_biovolume_mm3 * vol2massC) %>% 
  
  
  # Option 3: Lucie's coefficient for conversion is 0.9 (20% wet weight, 45% carbon in dry weight). Not that this is calculated from area and not volume
  # mutate(structural_carbon = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 0.2 * 0.45) %>%  # Ikeda et al., 1989
  
  # Option 3.2 for lower C%WW
  mutate(structural_carbon = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 0.0766) %>%  # 7.66% if based on C%WW of calanoids exceptt Arctic lipid forming species
  mutate(prosome_mgC_Bourreau = structural_carbon + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
# ** Note that wax ester mass is used here but Lucie's code seems to use lipid area/volume and multiplied with 0.79 Tarling et al. (2022) coefficient
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon
  mutate(
    LF_carbon_Jonasdottir = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_Jonasdottir * 100,
    LF_carbon_McConville = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_McConville * 100,
    LF_carbon_Bourreau = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_Bourreau * 100)


# *** For the manually segmented images ***
manual.segmented.images <- manual.segmented.images %>% 
  rename(prosome = prosomeManual, lipid = lipidManual,
         prosomeMajor = prosomeMajorManual,
         lipidMajor = lipidMajorManual) %>% 
  
  mutate(prosome_length_mm = prosomeMajor * uvpRes) %>% # based on segmentation
  
   # Convert pixel area to mm2
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome * uvpRes * uvpRes) %>% 
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome * uvpRes * uvpRes) %>% 
  
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis (in pixels)
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome / (pi * prosomeMajor/2)) * 2) %>% 
  mutate(minor_lipid_derived = (lipid / (pi * lipidMajor/2)) * 2) %>% 
  
  
  # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * (prosomeMajor/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation. According to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipidMajor * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
  # # Calculate lipid sac volume based spheroid (results in slightly larger volume)
  # mutate(lipid_volume_mm3_sph = 
  #          4/3 * pi * (lipidMajor/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_lipid_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2))

  
  # Calculate lipid fullness based on volume
  mutate(lipidfullness_volume  = (lipid_volume_mm3/prosome_biovolume_mm3 * 100)) %>% 
  
  # (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. 2010 with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  # TODO Updated 20251126 : should be based on volume, not area?? Similar to Lucie's calculation
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
  
  # TODO CLARIFY Calculate prosome carbon weight (** NOTE: many options ***)

  # Option 1: Use prosome length to volume (mm3) and calculate dry weight and mg C (Jonasdottir et al. 2019 for C. finmarchicus)
  mutate(prosome_volume_Jonasdottir = 
           0.0292 * (prosomeMajor * uvpRes)^3.6699,
         prosome_dryweight_Jonasdottir = 
           0.0106 * (prosomeMajor * uvpRes)^3.64,
         prosome_mgC_Jonasdottir = 
           0.623 * prosome_dryweight_Jonasdottir - 0.0143) %>% 
  
    # Option 2: Direct biovolume --> carbon mass based on conversion factors in McConville et al. 2016 assuming 1 mm3 = 1 mg wet weight
  mutate(prosome_mgC_McConville = 
           prosome_biovolume_mm3 * vol2massC) %>% 
  
  
  # Option 3: Lucie's coefficient for conversion is 0.9 (20% wet weight, 45% carbon in dry weight). Not that this is calculated from area and not volume
  # mutate(structural_carbon = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 0.2 * 0.45) %>%  # Ikeda et al., 1989
  
  mutate(structural_carbon = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 0.07) %>%  # Option 2 of lower C%WW
  
  # mutate(structural_carbon = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 0.0766) %>%  # 7.66% if based on C%WW of calanoids exceptt Arctic lipid forming species
  
  mutate(prosome_mgC_Bourreau = structural_carbon + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
# ** Note that wax ester mass is used here but Lucie's code seems to use lipid area/volume and multiplied with 0.79 Tarling et al. (2022) coefficient
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon
  mutate(
    LF_carbon_Jonasdottir = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_Jonasdottir * 100,
    LF_carbon_McConville = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_McConville * 100,
    LF_carbon_Bourreau = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_mgC_Bourreau * 100) 
```


## Get LOKI trait values
- The lipid mass calculated for LOKI is using the same equation as the wax ester calculation (Vogedes et al. 2010).
- In the LOKI calculations, the factor for converting lipid dry mass to carbon mass is 0.79, which is 0.016 lower than the value of lambda used here. So need to adjust values to make the estimates comparable?

```{r}
loki.segmentations <- read.csv("data/LOKI_Bourreau_manuscript/merged_LOKI2013_ecotaxa_masks_features.csv") %>% 
 
# match trait names
  mutate(total_carbon = prosome_carbon_volume + total_lipids_ugC/1000,
         # lf_carbon = fullness_ratio_carbon_volume * 100,
         lf_carbon = total_lipids_ugC/1000 / total_carbon * 100,
         waxester_carbon = total_lipids_ugC / 1000) %>% 
  #  # Recalculated version (lipid carbon not based on the variable total_lipids_carbon_volume)
  # mutate(lf_carbon = waxester_carbon / (waxester_carbon + prosome_carbon_volume) * 100) %>% 
  select(object_id, object_annotation_category,
         prosome_length_mm = prosome_major_axis_mm,
         prosome_biovolume_mm3 = prosome_volume_mm3,
         structural_carbon = prosome_carbon_volume,
         waxester_carbon,
         total_carbon, lf_carbon) %>% 
  mutate(source = "LOKI segmented")
```

## Calculate diapause respiration rate and potential diapause duration 
```{r}
indiv_traits <- segmented.images %>% 
  select(object_id, object_annotation_category,
         prosome_length_mm,
         prosome_biovolume_mm3,
         structural_carbon,
         waxester_carbon = waxester_mass_mgC,
         total_carbon = prosome_mgC_Bourreau,
         lf_carbon = LF_carbon_Bourreau) %>%
  
  mutate(source = "CNN segmented") %>% 
  # Remove images with manual segmentations
  filter(object_id %notin% manual.segmented.images$object_id) %>% 
  
  # TODO remove anomalously low structural carbon values
  filter(structural_carbon > 0.05) %>% 
  
  # Add the manually segmented images
  bind_rows(manual.segmented.images %>% 
              select(object_id, 
                     prosome_length_mm,
                     prosome_biovolume_mm3,
                     structural_carbon,
                     waxester_carbon = waxester_mass_mgC,
                     total_carbon = prosome_mgC_Bourreau,
                     lf_carbon = LF_carbon_Bourreau) %>% 
              left_join(segmented.images %>% 
                          select(object_id, object_annotation_category),
                        by = "object_id") %>% 
              
              mutate(source = "Manually segmented")) %>% 
  
  # The LOKI values
  bind_rows(loki.segmentations) %>% 
  
  # Calculate diapause respiration rate and duration
  mutate(mass_ugC = structural_carbon * 1000) %>% 
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday = 
           (2.3*10^-7) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp(0.6 * (273.65-273)/ ((8.62*10^-5)*273.65*273))  * 86400) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day = 
           (0.8*waxester_carbon*1000)/(respirationRate_ugCday)) %>% 
  
  mutate(source = factor(source, 
                         levels = c("Manually segmented",
                                    "CNN segmented",
                                    "LOKI segmented")))
```

# FOR copepods without segmentations....
## The rest of the copepods
```{r}
# Establish minimum length threshold... lowest Major axis length of segmented images
# Aroung 1.6 mm
minLength <- min((other.copepods.traits %>% 
       filter(with_segmentation == "segmented"))$Major*uvpRes)



other.copepods.traits <- all.copepods.uvp6 %>% 
  # Remove not complete copepods
  filter(object_annotation_category %notin% c("antenna<Calanoida",
                                              "antenna<Copepoda",
                                              "dead<Copepoda",
                                              "copepoda eggs",
                                              "part<Copepoda")) %>% 
  # Remove copepods validated to NOT be calanus
  filter(object_annotation_category %notin% c("Cyclopoida", "Harpacticoida",
                                              "Heterorhabdidae", "Heterorhabdus",
                                              "Metridia", "Paraeuchaeta")) %>% 
  # Only include VALIDATED images
  filter(object_annotation_status == "validated") %>% 
  # only include taxa larger than the smallest segmented image
  filter((Major*uvpRes) >= minLength) %>% 
  
  mutate(with_segmentation = if_else(object_id %in% indiv_traits$object_id,
```

```{r}
ggplot(other.copepods.traits,
       aes(x = Area, 
           fill = with_segmentation, color = with_segmentation )) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clrs, name = "Data source") +
  scale_color_manual(values = clrs, name = "Data source") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  xlab("Area (mm2)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.title.y = element_blank())
  
# Conversion factor to get prosome biomass (mg C) from biovolume (mm3)
# ** Note only use this if Calanus **
vol2massC <- mean(c(0.14373,0.1177,0.1902)) # average of 3 Calanus species in (McConville et al. (2016)

# Calculate biovolume-based carbon content based on major and minor axis
other.copepods.traits <- other.copepods.traits %>% 
  # Calculate biovolume
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * (Major/2 * uvpRes) * ((Minor/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>%
  # Calculate carbon weight
    
  # Option 2: Direct biovolume --> carbon mass based on conversion factors in McConville et al. 2016 assuming 1 mm3 = 1 mg wet weight
  mutate(prosome_mgC_McConville = 
           prosome_biovolume_mm3 * vol2massC) %>% 
  
  # Option 3: Lucie's coefficient for conversion is 0.09 (20% wet weight, 45% carbon in dry weight). 
  # This version assumes that there is no lipid sac. 
  # A similar conversion factor is calculated when averaging the C%WW trait literature = 0.09075
  mutate(structural_carbon = prosome_biovolume_mm3 * 0.2 * 0.45)  # Ikeda et al., 1989
  

ggplot(other.copepods.traits, aes(x = prosome_mgC_McConville, y = structural_carbon)) +
  # geom_point() +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")


ggplot(other.copepods.traits,
       aes(x = structural_carbon, 
           fill = with_segmentation, color = with_segmentation )) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clrs, name = "Data source") +
  scale_color_manual(values = clrs, name = "Data source") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  xlab("Carbon weight (mg)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.title.y = element_blank())
  


# Get % segmented copepods in total carbon weight per sample
assemblage <- other.copepods.traits %>% 
  filter(with_segmentation == "others") %>% 
  select(object_id, sample_id, object_annotation_category, 
         Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_m3,
         prosome_length_mm = Major, 
         total_carbon = structural_carbon,
         with_segmentation) %>% 
  # TODO there are a few missing images (42 were excluded?)
  bind_rows(segmented.images %>% 
              mutate(total_carbon =  structural_carbon + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
              select(object_id, sample_id, object_annotation_category, 
                     Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_m3,
                     Major, prosome_length_mm,
                     total_carbon) %>% 
              mutate(with_segmentation = "segmented")) %>% 
  group_by(sample_id, with_segmentation, Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_m3) %>% 
  summarise(total_carbon = sum(total_carbon),
            mean_length = mean(prosome_length_mm),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  # Calculate total for the sample
  group_by(sample_id, Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_m3) %>% 
  mutate(sample_total = sum(total_carbon)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(perc_carbon = total_carbon / sample_total * 100)

ggplot(assemblage, aes(x = perc_carbon, fill = with_segmentation)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = clrs, name = "Data source") +
  scale_color_manual(values = clrs, name = "Data source") +
  xlab("Percent of total carbon") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.title.y = element_blank())

# integrate as carbon/m2 of each sample
# TODO double check since this might be wrong....
assemblage.integ <- assemblage %>% 
  # calculate carbon concentration / m3 at each depth bin. .. must account for zeros
  mutate(carbon_m3 = total_carbon / Sampled_volume_m3) %>% 
  group_by(sample_id, with_segmentation) %>% 
  summarise(carbon_m2 = mean(carbon_m3),
            carbon_m3_sum = sum(carbon_m3 * 5),
            max_depth = max(Depth_5m),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  group_by(sample_id) %>% 
  mutate(sample_total = sum(carbon_m2)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(perc_carbon_m2 = carbon_m2 / sample_total * 100)
  
ggplot(assemblage.integ, aes(x = with_segmentation, y = carbon_m2)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_y_log10()

ggplot(assemblage.integ, aes(x = with_segmentation, y = perc_carbon_m2)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_y_log10()
```
